Explore the QEMU source tree at /local/nick/qemu_v5 (Andes QEMU fork). I need to know exactly how ACE (Andes Custom Extension) is supported at RUNTIME. Search thoroughly (case-insensitive "ace" is too noisy - use word-ish patterns like "ACE", "libace", "ace_", "andes_ace", "-ace", "acetool", "eca", "copilot", "aceasim").

Answer these questions with file paths and line numbers:
1. What command-line option / CPU property / machine property enables ACE? (e.g. -cpu xxx,ace=..., -ace <file>, a -global, or a QEMU option table entry). Show the exact option name and how a user passes it.
2. What file does QEMU load for ACE (a .so? the .eca? something copilot generates)? Which API does it use (dlopen? which symbols)?
3. Which QEMU binary/target has it (qemu-system-riscv64?) and is it compile-time gated (meson option, CONFIG_xxx)?
4. Any docs/README in the tree about ACE usage, and any example command line.
5. Is there anything about ACE state migration/gdbstub (ACR registers etc.)? Just note briefly.

Also check if the build dir exists (e.g. /local/nick/qemu_v5/build*) and whether the built qemu-system-riscv64 there has the option (strings or --help output if runnable).

Be thorough. Report the exact runtime invocation recipe for running an ACE binary on this QEMU.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

# ACE (Andes Custom Extension) runtime support in `/local/nick/qemu_v5`

Fork: `gitea.andestech.com/RD-SW/qemu` (origin), current branch `hybrid`. There are also dedicated branches `origin/andes-v5-ACE` and `origin/andes-v5-ACE-gdb`. Built binaries exist and already contain ACE support (see below). QEMU version reports `9.2.0 (v9.2.0-401-g4581fc99a4)`.

## 1. Command-line option / CPU property that enables ACE

ACE is enabled via **CPU (`-cpu`) properties**, not a machine property, a bespoke `-ace` flag, or an option-table entry. There is no `-ace <file>` option.

Boolean ISA-extension properties — `target/riscv/cpu.c:3188-3190` (registered via `MULTI_EXT_CFG_BOOL`, all default `false`):
- `xandesace` → `cfg.ext_XAndesAce` (the master switch)
- `xandesaceextra` → `cfg.ext_XAndesAceExtra` (enables custom-0/1/2 opcodes in addition to custom-3)
- `xandesacemulti` → `cfg.ext_XAndesAceMulti` (multi-ACE / multi-instance)

String properties — `target/riscv/cpu.c:4341-4348` (in `andes_cpu_property[]`):
- `xandesacelib` → `cfg.XAndesAceLib` — **path to the shared library QEMU dlopen()s** (required when `xandesace` is on)
- `xandesaceextlibpath` → `cfg.XAndesAceExtLibPath` — extra library search path passed through to the agent's `ace_agent_register`

Also note a separate Andes-config knob `isa-ace` (`target/riscv/csr_andes.c:1315`, sample default `off` in `docs/config/andes.cfg:38`) which sets the hardware capability bit `MMSC_CFG.ACE`. You do NOT need to set this manually: when `xandesace` is on, QEMU force-sets `MMSC_CFG.ACE=1` automatically at `target/riscv/csr_andes.c:1474-1477`.

Validation that ties it together: `target/riscv/tcg/tcg-cpu.c:834-863` (`riscv_cpu_validate_andes_ace`) — if `ext_XAndesAce` is set but `XAndesAceLib` is NULL it errors `"Invalid configuration: Andes ACE requires XAndesAceLib setting"`.

How a user passes it (example CPUs that support the props are the `andes-*` models, e.g. `andes-nx45v`, confirmed present in `-cpu help`):
```
-cpu andes-nx45v,xandesace=true,xandesacelib=/path/to/libace_model.so
```
Optionally add `,xandesaceextra=true`, `,xandesacemulti=true,xandesaceextlibpath=<dir>`.

`docs/config/andes.cfg` and `tests/andes_v5_tests/local_andes.cfg` document the equivalent `-global`/`-readconfig` form, e.g. `local_andes.cfg:11`: `# The same with '-cpu andes-nx45v,xandesaceextlibpath=lib'`.

## 2. What file is loaded and which API

- QEMU loads the **shared object (.so)** given by `xandesacelib` using **`dlopen(filename, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL)`** — `target/riscv/andes_ace_helper.c.inc:36` (`qemu_ace_agent_load`). Symbols are resolved with **`dlsym`** in `qemu_ace_agent_load_symbol` (`:43-55`).
- This .so is the "ACE Agent" produced by Andes' COPILOT/acetool flow (the tool that also generates the `.eca`); QEMU itself does not read a `.eca` — it talks to the agent library. The library version is negotiated: QEMU requires `ACE_AGENT_VERSION 102` (`target/riscv/ace-helper.h:18`) via the `ace_agent_version` symbol; there is also a `ace_agent_copilot_version` symbol (`ace-helper.h:104`).
- Symbols QEMU pulls from the .so (all in `target/riscv/andes_ace_helper.c.inc` / `ace-helper.h`):
  - `ace_agent_version`, `ace_agent_register`, `ace_agent_run_insn`, `ace_agent_get_register`, `ace_agent_set_register`, `ace_agent_get_packet`, `ace_agent_copilot_version`.
- Registration passes a **callback table** back to the library so the model can read/write QEMU CPU state: `ace_agent_cb_func_table[]` at `andes_ace_helper.c.inc:12-25` — get/set XRF, FRF, VRF, MEM, CSR (+masked), ACM, PC, hart id, priv, ACES, and `add_reg_desc`. Enum of callback slots: `ace-helper.h:20-41`.
- Runtime instruction execution: decoded ACE opcodes (`target/riscv/XAndesAce.decode`, custom-0/1/2/3 = opcodes 0001011/0101011/1011011/1111011) call `gen_helper_andes_ace` (`insn_trans/trans_xandesace.c.inc:17-31`), whose helper `helper_andes_ace` (`target/riscv/andes_helper.c:214-244`) calls `qemu_ace_agent_run_insn` → the library's `ace_agent_run_insn`. Return code 5 raises a local `ACEERR` interrupt; other nonzero raises illegal-instruction. Gating at translate time: `REQUIRE_ACE` (checks `MMSC_CFG.ACE`) + `REQUIRE_ACES` (checks `MMISC_CTL.ACES`) — `trans_xandesace.c.inc:7-13`.

## 3. Which binary/target, and compile-time gating

- Present in **both** RISC-V targets: system emulation `qemu-system-riscv64` and Linux-user `qemu-riscv64` (also the rv32 variants). Confirmed by `strings` on `build/qemu-system-riscv64` and `build/qemu-riscv64` — both contain `xandesace`, `xandesacelib`, `qemu_ace_agent_register`, `ace_agent_register`, etc.
- The user-mode paths are handled with `#ifdef CONFIG_USER_ONLY` branches throughout `andes_ace_helper.c.inc` (hartid=0, `cpu_ld*_data` instead of `_ra`, ACM no-ops).
- **Not gated by a meson feature option or a dedicated `CONFIG_XXX`.** It is compiled unconditionally into the riscv target. The only build-system touch is linking `-ldl` for `dlopen`: `meson.build:685-686` (`qemu_ldflags += ['-ldl']`, comment "For Andes ACE support since uses dysyn/dlopen"). Effective enablement is purely runtime via the CPU properties above. It is guarded at runtime by the `ext_XAndesAce` cfg flag and the `MMSC_CFG.ACE`/`MMISC_CTL.ACES` CSR bits.

## 4. Docs / README / example command lines in the tree

- No dedicated ACE `.rst`/`README` doc. The example command lines live in config samples:
  - `docs/config/andes.cfg` (header usage block, lines 1-15; `isa-ace = "off"` at line 38). Header shows: `qemu-system-riscv64 -M andes_ae350 -cpu [andes-nx45v|...] -readconfig andes.cfg`.
  - `tests/andes_v5_tests/local_andes.cfg:11,14` — documents `-cpu andes-nx45v,xandesaceextlibpath=lib`.
- Header comments in the source files (`target/riscv/ace-helper.h`, `andes_ace_helper.h`, `andes_ace_helper.c.inc`, `gdbstub/andes_ace_gdb.c.inc`) are the primary "documentation."

## 5. Migration / gdbstub (ACR/ACM registers) — brief

- **gdbstub: yes, substantial.** `target/riscv/gdbstub.c`:
  - `riscv_gen_dynamic_ace_xml` (`:395`) dynamically builds GDB target-description XML for ACR/ACM registers from `env->ace_acr_info_list` (populated by the agent via the `add_reg_desc` callback, `andes_ace_helper.c.inc:462`).
  - `andes_ace_get_reg`/`andes_ace_set_reg` (`:290`,`:331`) and `riscv_gdb_get_ace`/`set_ace` read/write ACR values through `qemu_ace_agent_get_register`/`set_register`. Registered as a coprocessor in `riscv_cpu_gdb_init` (`:535-540`).
  - `gdbstub/andes_ace_gdb.c.inc` implements the Andes `qRcmd` monitor commands (`nds query target/endian/cpuid`, `nds ace ...`). The `nds ace` command writes the agent's `get_packet` blob to a temp file whose name is the byte length (mimicking ICEman), via `qemu_ace_get_filename_for_gdb` (`andes_ace_helper.c.inc:420-460`). CPU-side state fields: `env->ace_acr_info_list`, `ace_acracm_reg_number`, `ace_acr_value`, `dyn_ace_feature` (`target/riscv/cpu.h:508-555`).
- **State migration (VMState/snapshots): essentially none.** `target/riscv/machine.c` has no ACE handling (grep found nothing). The ACR/ACM register state lives inside the external model library, not in QEMU's migratable `CPURISCVState`, so it is not part of the migration stream. The related interrupt bit `MIP_ANDES_ACEERR` is normal MIP/MIE plumbing (`cpu_helper.c:573-608`, `csr.c:3156`) and would migrate with the standard CSRs, but the custom ACR/ACM contents do not.

## Runtime invocation recipe (to run an ACE binary)

System mode:
```
qemu-system-riscv64 \
  -M andes_ae350 \
  -cpu andes-nx45v,xandesace=true,xandesacelib=/abs/path/libace_model.so \
  [-cpu ...,xandesaceextra=true]   # if you use custom-0/1/2 opcodes \
  [-cpu ...,xandesacemulti=true,xandesaceextlibpath=/abs/dir]  # multi-ACE \
  -bios <fw> -kernel <ace_binary> ...
```
Linux-user mode:
```
qemu-riscv64 -cpu andes-nx45v,xandesace=true,xandesacelib=/abs/path/libace_model.so ./ace_program
```
Requirements/behavior:
- `xandesacelib` must point to a valid Andes ACE Agent `.so` exporting `ace_agent_version` (>= 102), `ace_agent_register`, `ace_agent_run_insn`, etc.; otherwise QEMU aborts with `"xandesacelib '%s' cannot be loaded"` or `"... register failed"` (`tcg-cpu.c:849-859`).
- Setting `xandesace=true` auto-sets `MMSC_CFG.ACE`. At runtime the guest software must also set `MMISC_CTL.ACES` before executing ACE instructions (enforced by `REQUIRE_ACES`), otherwise the ACE insn traps.
- For GDB debugging of ACR/ACM, connect gdb with `-s -S`; the ACE register XML and `nds ace` rcmd support are automatic once the agent lib is loaded.

Key files: `target/riscv/andes_ace_helper.c.inc` (dlopen/dlsym + callbacks), `target/riscv/andes_ace_helper.h`, `target/riscv/ace-helper.h` (agent ABI/version), `target/riscv/cpu.c:3188-3190,4341-4348` (properties), `target/riscv/tcg/tcg-cpu.c:834-863` (load+register), `target/riscv/csr_andes.c:1474-1477` (MMSC_CFG.ACE), `target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_xandesace.c.inc` + `target/riscv/XAndesAce.decode` + `target/riscv/andes_helper.c:214-244` (execution), `target/riscv/gdbstub.c` + `gdbstub/andes_ace_gdb.c.inc` (ACR/ACM gdb), `meson.build:685-686` (`-ldl`).
